name: Callirhoe

project_scope.selection_mode: Four already installed canonical species; genus lesson backfill only
project_scope.source_pool: Genus Study Index row 68; existing species records in content/taxa/Malvaceae/Callirhoe

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: First turn a flower bud sideways and examine the calyx/extra bractlet region. The epicalyx (involucel) of C. involucrata is well-documented, but DO NOT use a blanket 'involucel absent in pedata' rule: FNA says absent, while UT's Williamson County C. pedata treatment says three bracteoles. Mark pedata anatomy taxonomic-review pending. Then inspect whether bud sepal tips converge or diverge, trailing versus erect habit, leaf stipules, and mature segmented fruit rather than relying on flower color.
shared_traits: Mallow flowers with five petals and many stamens fused into a staminal column around the style; alternate stipulate leaves.
Leaves can be deeply palmately lobed, but leaf division alone does not reliably split the erect species.
Dry segmented schizocarps composed of individual mericarps; mericarp dehiscence, beaks and collar shape are highly informative.
Presence/absence of involucellar bractlets, bud calyx behavior and fruit architecture provide more confidence than flower color.
shared_genus_recognition.visual_glossary: The involucel is an extra ring of typically three small bracts outside and just beneath the true five-lobed calyx; it is NOT a sixth sepal or a petal.

overlap_and_cautions: C. digitata is retained as a comparison/teaching concept: existing canonical species record notes current Kew/FNA ranges place true C. digitata outside Texas. Do NOT infer project-target nativity from its presence in this module.
C. pedata and C. digitata have both been confused in historical literature, including the name C. digitata var. stipulata; accepted-concept mapping belongs to taxonomy lane.
C. leiocarpa has historical misidentifications as C. pedata; mature dehiscent mericarps and annual habit are safer than petal color.
C. involucrata is variable at variety level; do not force an infraspecific ID from flower shade.
Involucel bractlets can lie flat against sepals, especially in open flowers; check unopened buds and take a lateral close-up.
Leaf lobes and stem height overlap across species and mowing may affect habit; preserve juvenile-versus-adult context.
Do not handle rare/nonlocal comparison taxa as locally confirmed natives without independent county evidence. Species range labels already in the canonical records are unchanged.

BOTANICAL SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: FNA C. pedata lacks involucellar bractlets and has racemose inflorescences, while UT Williamson County description reports three bracteoles under the calyx and paniculate flowers. The genus key must not force presence/absence based on this concept until verified independently.

Confirm number and arrangement of involucellar bracts, calyx, staminal column, leaf shape and mature schizocarp mericarps; some have superficially mallow-like flowers and hairy foliage.

local_lookalike_routing.separator: Show fruit and calyx/epicalyx detail: Hibiscus often has a true capsule rather than Callirhoe's dry mericarp ring; color alone is misleading.

look_here_first: FIRST turn a bud/flower SIDEWAYS and inspect the region immediately UNDER the true five-lobed CALYX for an extra ring of tiny BRACTLETS (INVOLUCEL/EPICALYX). On C. involucrata, three bractlets are strongly supported and buds have separated sepal tips. BUT do not use 'bractlets absent' as an unqualified C. pedata veto: FNA describes them absent, whereas UT's detailed Williamson County treatment describes three bracteoles on a plant identified C. pedata. This conflict needs independent taxonomic/specimen-photo review. SECOND check trailing versus erect habit and leaf/stipule characters. THIRD confirm annuality and ripe MERICARP anatomy (dehiscent vs indehiscent; beak/collar). Petal color is not sufficient.

genus_diagnostics.flower: Find five separate PETALS and the many ANTHERS carried on a central fused STAMINAL COLUMN. The central projection is NOT a single giant stamen and the cup-shaped whole flower does not distinguish species.
genus_diagnostics.calyx: Inspect the green five-lobed CALYX immediately below the five colored petals. In C. involucrata its calyx lobes are usually divergent in bud (tips remain separated); in many congeners calyx lobe tips meet, creating a pointed VALVATE bud. A side-view of an unopened bud is a necessary confirmation.
genus_diagnostics.involucel: An INVOLUCEL (also called EPICALYX) is an extra ring of usually three smaller BRACTLETS below the CALYX, not part of the true sepal ring. FNA documents bractlets in C. involucrata and no bractlets in C. pedata/leiocarpa; HOWEVER a UT Williamson County description explicitly reports three bracteoles in C. pedata, so the C. pedata polarity is an authoritative-source conflict. Do not force an ID using a supposed absence unless a voucher/photo confirms the concept.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Look at the alternating, stipulate leaves. Individual blades are commonly PALMATELY LOBED (veins and lobes radiate from one point); lobe number overlaps. C. pedata has persistent stipules, and C. digitata often loses stipules; C. leiocarpa typically has auriculate stipules. A leaf picture seldom proves stipule form on its own.
genus_diagnostics.habit: C. involucrata is typically spreading or decumbent (trailing). C. leiocarpa is usually an annual/biennial, upright or weakly erect. C. pedata and digitata are perennials with often erect stems. Flowering posture can be affected by mowing, grazing and site conditions.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: The mallow ovary matures as a dry SCHIZOCARP: a ring of individual wedge-like MERICARPS. Leiocarpa usually has fruit segments that OPEN (dehiscent), with beaks and prominent collars; pedata and involucrata are usually indehiscent. Only a ripe, focused fruit macro can verify the distinction; a developing green fruit photo cannot.
genus_diagnostics.stipules: STIPULES are small appendages in PAIRS at the base of each leaf petiole, not the same as flower bractlets under the calyx. On digitata they are usually early-shed; on leiocarpa often broader and auriculate (earlike base); on pedata persistent and generally narrow—note UT Williamson records wider asymmetric stipules and panicles, complicating this historical concept.
genus_diagnostics.stem: Alternate leaf-bearing mallow stems; strongly trailing stems support winecup while taller erect/branching stems point to pedata/leiocarpa/digitata but never prove them.

shared_traits: Mallow flowers with five petals and many stamens fused into a staminal column around the style; alternate stipulate leaves.
Leaves can be deeply palmately lobed, but leaf division alone does not reliably split the erect species.
Dry segmented schizocarps composed of individual mericarps; mericarp dehiscence, beaks and collar shape are highly informative.
Presence/absence of involucellar bractlets, bud calyx behavior and fruit architecture provide more confidence than flower color.
The extra involucel/epicalyx bractlets are not the same as STIPULES at a foliage leaf base; this distinction is a high-value family-versus-genus terminology lesson.

visual_comparison.title: Callirhoe: under the calyx, then the bud and ripe fruit
visual_comparison.subtitle: Five physical exact-species learner photographs illustrate flower, whole habit, foliage, developing fruits and bud context. Missing C. digitata and C. leiocarpa rights-safe installed images are NOT silently replaced by external copyrighted photos.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: PETALS → CALYX (five green sepals) → possible INVOLUCEL (extra bractlets beneath) → LEAF STIPULES (different structure) → ripe MERICARPS. C. involucrata is typically trailing and bractleted. Other local species require bud/stipule/fruit confirmation; C. pedata involucel descriptions conflict between references.

items.label: Trailing winecup: whole patch and palmate foliage
items.creator: Stan Shebs
items.caption: Find stems spreading sideways through the patch, with multiple palmately lobed leaves. This shows HABIT rather than the critical involucel close-up; do not treat trailing habit alone as decisive.

items.label: Winecup: five petals and central column
items.creator: Clinton & Charles Robertson
items.caption: Five showy magenta PETALS form the cup. The pale center is the column of fused STAMENS and styles common to local mallows. A straight-on front view is poor for counting the tiny bractlets UNDER the calyx.

items.label: Winecup: leaves with developing fruit
items.creator: Nadiatalent
items.caption: Find the leaf outline with lobes radiating from its base. Fruiting material is present with foliage but the photograph does not serve as a verified dissection of ripe mericarps, their beaks, or collars.

items.label: Palmleaf poppymallow: upright flowers and foliage
items.creator: lanechaffin
items.caption: Compare the taller upright to weakly erect flower-bearing stems and divided palmately lobed leaves against trailing C. involucrata. The leaf can have narrow segments; its silhouette can overlap digitata.

items.label: Palmleaf poppymallow: flower and bud
items.image_role: flower and unopened bud side context
items.creator: giantcicada
items.caption: Find an OPEN flower and a neighboring BUD. Bud shape is the next diagnostic clue: confirm whether the CALYX tips meet at the top. This installed photograph is context, NOT an audited involucel/bractlet macro; competing descriptions of pedata need review.

comparison_cards.title: C. involucrata vs C. pedata
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Spreading perennial versus commonly erect perennial: compare WHOLE PLANT first, then buds and ripe fruits. C. involucrata has a documented three-bractlet epicalyx and nonpointed separated calyx tips. FNA says pedata has no involucel, BUT UT Williamson County records pedata with three bracteoles; mark that particular separator uncertain until a voucher and photo review.
photo_requirements: same-scale flower bud side views exposing true calyx/epicalyx
side-by-side full habit and leaf/stipule photos
comparison_cards.caution: Do not overcall a pedata ID from apparent involucel absence; authoritative conflict under review.

comparison_cards.title: C. leiocarpa vs C. pedata
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Erect annual/biennial versus perennial; find the leaf's pair of STIPULES, then ripe fruit MERICARPS. Leiocarpa's distinct opening dehiscent mericarps, beak and collar are a stronger split than flower color.
photo_requirements: external-reference-only plants need new licensed installed exact photos
ripe dehiscent vs indehiscent mericarps with ruler
comparison_cards.caution: Unlicensed external nursery images are not installed photographs; stage and rights must be respected.

comparison_cards.title: C. digitata vs C. pedata
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both may have fingerlike divided leaves. Digitata is an out-of-target-range comparison with more narrowed many-lobed foliage and commonly early-shed stipules. Pedata's accepted concept typically has persistent stipules; historic Texas usage can overlap names and descriptions.

leaf base stipules; mature fruit; overall inflorescence from wild accession
